o: State the purpose of the Data Protection Act 2018.
Explain duties when collecting, using and keeping personal data.
Identify practices that could compromise data protection.
c: The UK Data Protection Act 2018 sits alongside the UK GDPR framework and protects individuals when organisations handle personal data. Organisations must have a lawful basis for processing.
Tell people why their data is collected and use it for clear, legitimate purposes. Collect no more personal information than is necessary for that purpose.
Keep personal data accurate and up to date where needed. Do not retain identifiable information longer than necessary for the purpose.

Apply appropriate protection, limit access and respect applicable rights to access or correct their information. A lost unencrypted device with pupil records can create a serious data-protection risk.

m.title: Collect only necessary trip details
m.q: A school trip form asks for a pupil's medical needs, emergency contact and favourite television programme. Explain TWO data-protection concerns. [4 marks]
st: Identify the trip's legitimate purpose: safety and communication.
Emergency and medical information may be necessary [1] to support safe trip management [1].
A favourite television programme is not relevant [1], so collecting it breaches the aim of data minimisation [1].
Use precise language: collect data that is necessary for a specified legitimate purpose.

w: A sports club stores members' home addresses indefinitely after cancellation. Explain the data-protection concern and an improvement. [4 marks]

Personal data should not be kept longer than needed [1], so indefinite retention without a valid purpose is inappropriate [1]. The club should set a justified retention period [1] and securely delete records once no longer required [1].
A council website uses an out-of-date address for a resident. Explain one duty relating to data accuracy and how the error could affect the resident. [4 marks]

The organisation must take reasonable steps to keep personal information accurate [1] and correct inaccuracies when identified [1]. An old address [1] could cause important correspondence to go to the wrong place [1].
A hospital stores unencrypted patient records on a shared laptop. Explain TWO ways it could improve security. [4 marks]
Encrypt stored records [1], so a stolen laptop does not expose readable files without a key [1]. Restrict accounts and permissions [1], so only authorised staff can access the patient data [1].

k.q: Simulate a check that avoids storing an extra personal detail when it is not needed.
k.code:
needed = 0
if needed == 1 then
    print("Collect this field")
else
    print("Do not collect")
endif
p: Change needed to 1 and explain the new output.
Add print("State the purpose") after the IF statement.
k.a:
With needed = 0: Do not collect. With needed = 1: Collect this field.

Extended OCR ERL:
needed = 1
if needed == 1 then
    print("Collect this field")
else
    print("Do not collect")
endif
print("State the purpose")

Real data protection also requires a lawful basis and transparency; this example demonstrates only a simulated minimisation check.

A school app requests pupils' names, emergency contacts and favourite music. Explain TWO data-protection responsibilities when collecting this information. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official OCR past paper.
Identify and communicate a lawful, specific purpose [1], so people know why data is collected [1]. Minimise personal information collected [1], avoiding unnecessary items such as favourite music [1].

Describe THREE ways a company should protect personal data under UK data-protection requirements. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official OCR past paper.

Use a lawful purpose and tell data subjects about processing [2]. Keep information accurate, correcting known errors [2]. Store it securely through limited permissions/encryption [2]. Other appropriate duties, such as minimisation or retention limits, may be credited.

r: State TWO environmental concerns linked to digital technology. [2 marks]
E-waste from discarded devices [1] and electricity/energy consumption [1]. Other clear valid concerns include manufacturing emissions or extracting raw materials.

A doctor encrypts confidential files on a portable drive. Explain TWO reasons this helps keep information private. [4 marks]

Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext [1], preventing straightforward reading [1]. A decryption key is needed [1], so losing the drive does not automatically expose readable records [1].

priorExam.q: A secondary school moves all homework online. Explain one benefit and one social disadvantage. [4 marks]
priorExam.a: Homework can be accessed anywhere with Internet [1], making resources easy to distribute/submit [1]. Pupils without reliable devices or connectivity [1] may find it harder to complete work, widening inequality [1].
